text:
maia: heads-up: on today's long-run shadow we noticed reproducible drift when KV cache is restored after a garbage-collect window. affects fp8 variants primarily for long-code and legal prompts. posting quick notes and a short hypothesis.
oscar: saw that too. interestingly the drift appears only when restore triggers a re-quant path instead of a load-from-disk path. small per-token diffs accumulate.
lee_runtime: runtime traces show a re-quant path executed after kv-restore where we do per-tensor stochastic rounding. the seed changes on restore -> tiny bias. over long ctx this biases beam choices.
maia: eval-bot examples:
```
family=legal-multi-clauses id=lm-772
baseline(fp8): acceptability=0.92
restore-requant(fp8): acceptability=0.86
delta= -6 pts, mostly hallucination types
```
kai: could this be numerical noise inherent to fp8 + stochastic rounding? or is it our implementation (seed handling) making it worse?
oscar: i ran deterministic rounding patch (round-to-nearest) and drift dropped by ~60% but latency increased ~3ms. tradeoff.
lee_runtime: another axis: layer-selective fallback. attention layers seem more sensitive to rounding noise than feed-forward. we could fallback only MLP -> int8 or attention -> int8 depending on metric. cheap to implement: per-layer flags in kernel table.
taylor_ops: ops question: storage/telemetry - do we want to persist per-request "requant_path" and "requant_seed"? storage budget is tight but this would let us correlate seed->drift.
maia: yes for diagnostics but keep it sampled. 1/500 requests store full seed+layer-map; aggregated hourly counters otherwise.
eval-bot: offline sweep summary:
- fp8 baseline vs deterministic-rounding: median quality delta -0.5% (improved)
- fp8 fallback-mlp->int8: median delta +0.3% vs baseline, runtime +1.8ms
- fp8 fallback-attn->int8: median delta +0.9%, runtime +2.4ms
recommendation: prefer mlp-only int8 fallback for quick, low-latency fixes.
kai: also a behavioral idea: when we do a restore->requant, tag the request header X-Quant-Event:kv-restore and open a 1-off shadow comparison locally for next N=3 requests. cheap sample to detect whether this restore is noisy and only then escalate to per-layer fallback.
oscar: agree. that avoids unnecessary fallbacks on benign restores. we should also add a small cooldown to avoid thrashing when restores happen frequently.
lee_runtime: kernel-note: changing layer precision mid-request is OK for some backends, but others need kernel rebinding which blocks for ~12-20ms. for latency SLO routes, prefer routing to an already warmed INT8 path rather than rebinding. we can implement a quick-check: if estimated rebind cost > 10ms and route p95 < 150ms, choose routing instead.
taylor_ops: add route config flag quant_rebind_policy = [prefer_rebind|prefer_route|no_autofallback]. expose via customer config API and allow header override for internal canaries.
maia: security/compliance: some enterprise customers forbid dynamic precision changes. we need a policy enforcement check at request ingress and deny header override unless customer permits.
ei-bot: (typo) eval-bot: scheduled noisy-restore canary for one internal non-prod route next Tue 09:00 PT. will collect sampled seeds and layer fallback counters.
maia: action items: 1) lee - add per-request kv-restore tag + sampled seed capture (3 days) 2) oscar - implement deterministic-rounding toggle + mlp-only fallback (4 days) 3) taylor - add route-level quant_rebind_policy + customer enforcement (5 days) 4) kai - prepare eval harness sets and automated small-sample shadow (3 days)
oscar: i'll also add a microbench for rebind cost per-backend and expose as runtime metric rebind_latency_ms.
lee_runtime: timeline sounds good. i'll include cooldown/hysteresis: exponential backoff per-endpoint starting at 30s.
taylor_ops: planning canary and runbook. adding storage budget note: sampled seeds + layer maps stored 7 days by default for canary.
maia: thanks everyone. let's reconvene after canary results. try to keep the deterministic rounding toggle behind a feature flag so we can A/B test. :thumbsup:
